V4.why: Step 1: the rule must be judged by one writer per partition. Step 2: under R lww any replica accepts a conditional write on its own state, so two sells of the last item through two servers both pass. Step 3: v4 measured exactly that: both ok (REQUIREMENTS P-14, DESIGN-V5 9).

BUY.why: Step 1: BUY's only condition is JetStream's 'expected last sequence of this subject', and a row is one subject. Step 2: so a rule over a partition of several rows cannot be judged as one; the only wider check is the whole stream's last sequence, which any other write breaks (E-44 gap 4, reasoned from the headers). Step 3: the judge is the client, not the one writer: it reads, computes and retries (about 4 ms an op, 34 % of publishes wasted at 8 writers). For one row at a time it holds: one ok in 100 of 100 rounds.

default.why: With A-24 (locks belong to the unit; a failed run undoes every step) E-24's model holds all-or-nothing, no G0 and 'every unit ends' on seven bounds, each explored in full, up to 2.9 million states, with a crash at every step and a paused holder (41 of 44 mutants caught).
